newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - BA fights rival for French Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BA fights rival for French Air Liberte.

text.p: British Airways Plc on Friday appealed to European Commissioners to intervene "with utmost urgency" to block a French plan to sell troubled regional airline Air Liberte to another French-owned airline, AOM.
BA had said earlier in the day that it was interested in Air Liberte's assets, which administrators may sell off.
"Allowing AOM to buy Air Liberte would be an illegal use of state aid," British Airways said in its letters to Europe's Transport and Competition Commissioners.

In a company statement, BA explained that it was basing its objection on AOM's current status -- the airline is for sale because it is a unit of troubled bank group Credit Lyonnais, which is being restructured with a huge tranche of state aid.

BA chief executive Bob Ayling was quoted as saying the sale would be against European rules on state aid "because it would add further to the liabilities facing the AOM group, in contravention of the conditions of the Credit Lyonnais aid".

The British company, meanwhile, is examining the potential for buying Liberte to add to its current French subsidiary airline, TAT European Airlines. BA said it had explained to the commissioners that any bid for Liberte "would be consistent with BA's efforts during the past three years to keep competition alive in France".
Michael Blunt, BA's public relations manager, said: "TAT has been in contact with the administrator to assess what he is looking to realise out of the remaining assets of Air Liberte."
In Paris, the newspaper Le Monde reported that TAT expected to make an offfer for Air Liberte "in the next few days" but Blunt said he was not aware of any urgency.
"There is no indication of any timetable as yet on this -- it's early days," he told Reuters by telephone.
Privately-owned Air Liberte was put into legal adminstration on September 26 after defaulting on payments.
What seems to have annoyed British Airways most is that, according to press reports, authorities have already approved a so-called "French solution" that will swallow up Air Liberte.
Le Monde said on Friday that Paris wanted to see the creation of a second force to Air France, built around a new French airline based on a fusion of AOM, Air Liberte and privately-owned Euralair.
If BA were to buy Air Liberte, on the other hand, it would stand to gain a valuable toe-hold on slots at Paris Orly airport.
"New slots at Orly are no longer available because of restrictions imposed by the French authorities," BA noted tersely in its statement.
For good measure, Le Monde reported that that BA was also in competition with its British arch-rival Virgin, which it said "is equally ready to make an offer to take over Air Liberte".
Reuters was not able to confirm this report during the day.

Depite being an attractive prize, Air Liberte is in poor shape. BA said the airline lost 650 million francs ($125 million) in the first nine months of this year and has total debts of about 1.5 billion francs.
Meanwhile, Liberte has begun a rescue plan that involves taking several large planes out of its fleet and cutting routes -- both long-haul to Africa and Canada and some internal ones.
The plan, under which it is cutting 285 jobs and focusing on medium- and short-haul flights, is to run for about six months. ($1=5.178 French Franc)
